item.statement: The continuous ordered B2 matrix in the initial microstructure causes poor ductility and limits engineering applications.
item.lever: microstructure inversion (changing continuous phase from B2 to BCC)
quotes: The poor ductility is attributed to the continuous matrix being the ordered B2 phase in these alloys.
While the B2 matrix provides a very high strength to this condition, it suffers from rather poor ductility due to its ordered nature.
resulting in limited compressive ductility.

item.statement: Existing ductility improvement methods like metastability engineering cannot be applied to inherently brittle RHEAs that fracture without strain localization.
quotes: Unfortunately, this method is only applicable to intrinsically ductile RHEAs that show low tensile ductility due to rapid strain localization and necking.
It cannot be applied to inherently brittle RHEAs that fracture without strain localization/necking and, often, without any macroscopic strain.
Unfortunately, the approaches for improving ductility discussed above cannot be applied to this class of Al-containing RHEAs.

item.statement: Achieving the highest strength (Condition 1) results in the lowest ductility, while achieving the highest ductility (Condition 2) results in significantly lower strength.
quotes: Condition (1) is stronger (but less ductile) than Condition (3) since the harder B2 phase is continuous in Condition (1) while the softer BCC phase is continuous in Condition (3).

item.statement: The exact phase stability and transformation mechanisms at 1400 °C remain uncertain, specifically whether phase separation occurs at this temperature.
quotes: Important details of the phase stabilities and phase transformations in this alloy remain uncertain.
However, it is possible that the alloy may be undergoing phase separation at 1400 °C.
These possibilities need to be studied in future work.

item.statement: The mechanism responsible for the anomalous strengthening (higher yield strength at 600 °C than at room temperature) in Condition (3) is not fully understood.
quotes: The data needed to establish the mechanism responsible for the anomalous strengthening measured for Condition (3) are difficult to obtain and are beyond the scope of the present work.
The discussion offered here is highly speculative.
The details of the deformation mechanisms at room temperature and at 600 °C for this RHEA require further investigation, and is recommended for future study.
